This is the pivotal finding. Two things now stand out sharply, and I need to verify a few more before I write.

1. **The "Raj Anand" contractor is the subject of a confirmed data-exfiltration finding** (Denise Carter's March 1 "Interim Security Findings," externally corroborated by Blue Peak on April 7): four off-hours VPN sessions from a Nashville TN IP in February, **CSV PII exports** on specific files **LN-2026-00184, -00211, -00237, -00244**, plus a 38-row bulk pipeline export on 2026-02-24 — and his admin access was never de-provisioned after the CRM project closed. His account shows "suspended 2026-03-01," yet a person named "Raj" is doing hands-on ransomware IR on March 20 and emailing on April 5. That's the same IT contractor Robert is leaning on for the restore read.

- **No written reply from cyber counsel (Megan Sloane / Ward Barrett) is on record** — the specific sanctions/OFAC read on paying 2 BTC that Robert requested Mar 20 appears still open (only an initial privileged call happened that night, which produced the notice/SAR/privilege framing).
- **Draft borrower notices already exist** (Denise, sitting in DRAFT, Apr 14) for the Evan Mercer post-termination matter — and they name **LN-2025-00002 (Adams), LN-2025-00007 (Perry), LN-2025-00229 (Turner)** — which conflicts with IT's log that said Evan's third file was **LN-2026-00009 (Singh)**. A real discrepancy.
- The **CRM engagements list is the "engagement log"** with existing incident notes.

Let me write the decision brief and preserve the counsel correspondence in a new incident folder.

input.content:
# PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — PREPARED AT DIRECTION OF COUNSEL
# Incident Decision Brief — Ransomware / Borrower-Data Exposure
**Prepared for:** Robert Calloway (Owner/Broker)
**Date:** 2026-04-28
**Matter:** LOS ransomware event (initial detection 2026-03-20) and related unauthorized-access workstreams
**Outside cyber counsel of record (this matter):** Megan Sloane, Ward Barrett Law (msloane@wardbarrettlaw.com)

> Purpose: reconcile the picture Robert has been operating on against what the emails, Slack, LOS/IT
> logs, and the external security memo actually say — so the pay-vs-restore call and the borrower-notice
> posture can be decided on facts, not on the Friday-night recollection. Where my read differs from the
> operating picture, it is called out in **bold** under "Where my read differs."

---

## 1. PAY vs. RESTORE

### 1a. What the records actually say (restore difficulty is CORROBORATED)
Robert's recollection of Raj's read that night holds up against the contemporaneous record. Every element checks out:

| Element (Robert's memory) | Source in the record | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Local backups encrypted/unusable | Raj Slack 3/20 "backup server is unavailable"; Robert→Sloane email 3/20 "local backups appear encrypted/unusable"; Denise→Sloane 3/20 "local backup server also appears encrypted"; Raj DRAFT "URGENT: LOS inaccessible" | Confirmed |
| Cloud copy ~3 days behind | Multiple 3/20 messages: cloud backup "~72 hrs old" | Confirmed |
| Rebuild + validation required | Raj Slack 3/22 "Rebuild infra first, then restore/validate… can't promise LOS integrity till tested" | Confirmed |
| File gaps for pipeline since snapshot | Raj "significant data re-entry"; Grace "pipeline gaps from last 3 days," "Monday closings already shaky" | Confirmed |

**Restore is a genuine lift, but it is not a foregone conclusion.** The specific, itemized tradeoffs:

**Restore path — cost/gaps:**
1. On-prem/local backup server is encrypted → no local restore point.
2. Only viable restore point is a cloud snapshot ~72h stale (best case Tuesday PM).
3. Environment/infrastructure must be rebuilt *before* restore.
4. Restore + full validation/testing needed; LOS data integrity unverifiable until tested.
5. ~3 days of pipeline activity between snapshot and encryption requires manual reconstruction from inboxes/manual docs.
6. Near-term ops drag: Monday closings shaky; team can triage but "not cleanly."

**Pay path (2 BTC) — cost/risk:**
1. **OFAC/sanctions exposure** — paying a sanctioned threat actor is itself unlawful; this is the exact read requested from counsel and, per the record, **not yet answered in writing** (see §3).
2. No guarantee a decryptor is delivered or works.
3. **Payment does not cure the legal exposure.** The core liability is potential NPPI exposure and the resulting notice/SAR duties — those exist whether or not the data is decrypted. Paying buys back operations, not the breach.
4. Funds a criminal enterprise; possible repeat targeting.

### 1b. Where my read differs — the source problem on the restore read
**The technical read underpinning "restore is too expensive, consider paying" comes from Raj Anand — the same IT contractor who is the subject of an active, externally-corroborated data-exfiltration finding.**
- Denise Carter's internal "Interim Security Findings" (3/1/2026) and Blue Peak Security's external memo (Megan Holt, 4/7/2026) both document Raj Anand's credentials used for off-hours LOS access from a Nashville, TN IP (73.214.188.41) across four February sessions, each with **CSV PII exports**, plus a 38-row bulk pipeline export on 2/24.
- His admin access (los_admin, reporting_export) was never de-provisioned after the CRM migration project closed (Nov 2025). Access history shows the account "suspended 2026-03-01" — **yet a person named "Raj" was running hands-on ransomware IR on 3/20 and emailing on 4/5**, which itself needs to be explained.

**Recommendation:** Do not treat Raj as the sole/independent voice on restore-vs-pay. The backup state is independently corroborated, so the *facts* stand — but get an independent forensic read (Blue Peak or a counsel-directed IR firm) before any payment decision, and preserve privilege over that work. This is the single biggest thing outside Robert's current operating picture.

**Bottom line on the call:** Restore, not pay, is the defensible default — the sanctions risk is unresolved, payment doesn't extinguish the notice exposure, and the restore tradeoffs (while real) are known and survivable. Hold any payment decision until (a) counsel's sanctions read is in writing and (b) an independent forensic read confirms/─rebuts the restore picture.

The restore picture holds up: local/on-prem backups are encrypted (no local restore point); the only viable restore point is a cloud snapshot ~72 hours stale; environment rebuild + validation is required; LOS integrity is unverifiable until tested; and ~3 days of pipeline activity needs manual reconstruction. So restore is a real lift — but not impossible. On the pay side, my concerns are (a) the sanctions/OFAC question, (b) no guarantee of a working decryptor, and (c) that paying 2 BTC does not extinguish our notice/SAR exposure, which turns on whether NPPI was accessed, not on whether we get our data back.

Open item for you: we asked for the sanctions/OFAC read on 3/20 and I don't have it in writing yet. I do not intend to authorize any payment until that read is in hand and an independent forensic firm (not our current IT contractor) has verified the backup/restore state and the encrypted-vs-exfiltrated question.

2) A source-integrity issue you should factor in.
The technical read behind "restore is costly" came from our IT contractor, Raj Anand — who is himself the subject of an active, externally-corroborated finding (our internal 3/1 memo and Blue Peak Security's 4/7 memo) of off-hours LOS access from an out-of-state IP and recurring CSV exports of borrower PII, on an admin account that was never de-provisioned. The backup facts are independently corroborated, so they stand, but I don't want our restore/pay decision resting on his characterization. I'd like the forensic verification to be counsel-directed to preserve privilege.

3) BORROWER NOTICE — scope has widened since March, not narrowed.
The 3/20 framing was ransomware-only with no file-level list. Since then, several separate-but-converging workstreams have produced concrete files, some with confirmed data egress that is stronger than anything the ransomware itself has shown:
- Contractor export (Raj Anand): CSV PII exports logged on LN-2026-00184, -00211, -00237, -00244, plus a 38-row bulk export. Confirmed egress. (Separate counsel, Laura Bennett/bennettcyberlaw, was engaged 4/7 on this.)
- Keisha lender-portal compromise: LN-2026-00522, -00008, -00010, -00009. Draft notices prepared 4/7, held for IT scope.

- Marcus Webb: four manual mailbox forwards to a personal address + bulk downloads (e.g., LN-2026-00608). Confirmed egress.
- Leo Park (intern): 34 unassigned file views incl. a high-profile borrower (LN-2026-00606); download/export still TBD.
All named files contain SSNs, tax returns/W-2s, and bank statements.

Questions for you:
a) Is restore the defensible default while the sanctions read and independent forensics are outstanding, and are there steps we must take now to preserve privilege around the payment-decision process?
b) Given confirmed NPPI egress in the contractor-export and Marcus workstreams, do our notice obligations now attach independent of the ransomware's encrypted-vs-exfiltrated question?
c) Should these workstreams be consolidated into a single borrower-notice population/theory, and should your firm and Bennett's coordinate so we notify once, correctly?
d) Where do we land on a FinCEN SAR — you flagged it as likely on 3/20 and it's still unresolved.
e) Anything you need from us to close the encrypted-vs-exfiltrated determination.

I'm holding all borrower notices (drafts stay in DRAFT) and any payment decision until I hear back. Happy to get on a privileged call today or tomorrow.

Robert Calloway
Owner / Broker, Keystone Mortgage Partners

All five deliverables are done. Here's the reconciled picture and what I put in motion.

## What I found — and where it differs from the picture you've been operating on

**Pay vs. restore — your memory of Raj's read checks out, but the framing has a problem.**
Every element you recalled is corroborated by the contemporaneous record (your own 3/20 email to Sloane, Raj's Slack updates, Grace's ops notes, Raj's unsent "URGENT" draft): local backups encrypted, cloud snapshot ~72h stale, environment rebuild + validation required, LOS integrity unverifiable until tested, ~3 days of pipeline needing manual re-entry. So **restore is a genuine lift — but not a foregone conclusion**, and the tradeoffs are known and survivable.

Two things I'd flag plainly:
- **The restore read came from Raj Anand — who is himself the subject of an active, externally-corroborated data-exfiltration finding** (Denise's 3/1 internal memo + Blue Peak's 4/7 external memo: off-hours LOS access from a Nashville IP, weekly CSV exports of borrower PII, on an admin account never de-provisioned). His account even shows "suspended 3/1," yet he was running IR on 3/20 and emailing on 4/5. Don't rest the pay/restore call on his sole characterization — get an independent, counsel-directed forensic read.
- **Paying 2 BTC doesn't solve the actual problem.** The liability is NPPI exposure/notice, which exists whether or not we decrypt. Plus the sanctions/OFAC read you asked Sloane for on 3/20 is **still not in writing.** My recommendation: restore is the defensible default; authorize no payment until the sanctions read lands and independent forensics verify the state.

**Borrower notice — scope has widened, not narrowed.**
Don't take the March ransomware-only framing at face value. There are now **six converging workstreams**, several with *confirmed* data egress (stronger than anything the ransomware itself shows): the Raj contractor exports (LN-2026-00184/-00211/-00237/-00244, confirmed CSV), Keisha's portal (00522/00008/00010/00009), Evan Mercer (drafts written but unsent), Marcus Webb's mailbox forwards (confirmed egress, LN-2026-00608), and Leo Park's 34 intern views incl. the high-profile file. All named files contain SSNs/tax docs/bank statements.

**Queued items you may not have been looped on:** three fully-drafted Evan-Mercer borrower notices sitting unsent in DRAFT; Keisha notice drafts held since 4/7; a *separate* cyber-counsel firm (Bennett) engaged for the contractor matter; and a real **discrepancy** — Evan's third file is logged as LN-2026-00009 by IT but named LN-2025-00229 in the drafted notice. Those must be reconciled before anything goes out.

## Actions taken
1. **Decision brief** written to `/audit/2026-03-ransomware-incident/decision_brief_ransomware_2026-04-28.md`, with the counsel correspondence preserved alongside it in the same folder.
2. **Emailed outside cyber counsel** (Megan Sloane, Ward Barrett Law; cc Denise) with the reconciled picture and five specific questions on the open items — privilege-marked.
3. **Leadership status** posted to the Grace/Robert/Denise channel (kept tight, not pushed wider).
4. **Formal note** added to the CRM engagement log for the incident record.

**What I deliberately did *not* do:** send any borrower notices or authorize/imply any payment — both drafts and the payment decision are held pending counsel sign-off and independent forensics, which is the defensible posture.

One judgment call worth confirming: I treated the leadership Grace/Robert/Denise group DM as the "leadership channel" (there's no dedicated leadership Slack channel, and #general would have been too wide). Say the word if you'd rather I post it elsewhere.
